biography.plain_text: John Paul Papanicolaou was a Greek shipping and property businessman who served as president of Titan Brokerage. His interests extended to Euro-Mediterranean Estates, a venture focused on tourism and residential projects in southern Europe. He worked with investment partners and maritime specialists on commercial projects involving the reuse of historic ships.

long_biography.plain_text:
For businessman John Paul Papanicolaou, maritime restoration was a commercial opportunity as well as a way to preserve history. Having known Aristotle Onassis through family connections, he saw a market for older craft whose past could distinguish them from new construction. He assembled outside investors and worked with naval architect Costas Carabelas to bring that approach into the charter market.

His demands centred on reconciling historic appearance with expanded guest accommodation. He supplied old photographs as references, insisted on retaining the exterior profile and worked with architect Apostolos Molindris on the interiors. The resulting restoration required extensive reconstruction, making the preservation of recognizable spaces a design priority.
